note: Training questions for the loan-file flight simulator. Product-line figures are the numbers in data/gse/*.json. They are not a commitment to lend and not DU, LPA, TOTAL, or GUS.

questions.title: Pre-flight: is this an application yet?
The six items
questions.brief: Regulation Z treats an application as six specific pieces of information.
questions.question: Which set is the six-item TRID application?

options.text: Name, income, SSN, property address, estimated value, and loan amount
W-2s, tax returns, bank statements, and a signed contract
Credit score, appraisal, title commitment, and homeowner's insurance

questions.explain: The six items are name, income, Social Security number, property address, estimated property value, and the loan amount sought. Supporting documents are collected around that, but they are not the six.

questions.title: Documents versus the six
questions.brief: The borrower has not uploaded tax returns yet.
questions.question: Do two years of W-2s have to be in the file before a TRID application exists?

options.text: No. W-2s are documents, not one of the six items
Yes. Without W-2s there is no application
Only if the loan is FHA

questions.explain: Income is one of the six. The paper that proves it can arrive later.

questions.title: Purchase contract
questions.brief: The property is identified, but the purchase contract is still with the agent.
questions.question: Is a signed purchase contract one of the six items that create the application?

options.text: Yes, it replaces the property address
Yes, but only for conventional loans

questions.explain: The address and estimated value are in the six. The contract is important to the file, and it is not part of the six-item definition.

questions.title: Which number counts
questions.brief: You have a credit score on the screen and no Social Security number yet.
questions.question: Which of these is one of the six application items?
questions.explain: The Social Security number is one of the six. A credit score and a gift letter are underwriting evidence, not the application trigger.

questions.title: Income before the stubs
questions.brief: The borrower stated income. Paystubs are not in yet.
questions.question: Does stated income count as the income item even if the stubs come later?

options.text: Yes. The income figure is the item; the documents support it
No. Income does not count until a W-2 is imaged

questions.explain: The application item is the income, not the imaging of the proof.

questions.title: Which property fact
questions.brief: You have a legal description from the listing and no street address.
questions.question: Which property fact is one of the six?

options.text: The legal description instead of an address

questions.explain: Property address is one of the six. A legal description and HOA papers do not replace it.

questions.title: Loan amount
questions.brief: The borrower asked for a specific loan amount.
questions.question: Is the loan amount sought one of the six application items?

options.text: No. Only the purchase price counts

questions.explain: Loan amount is the sixth item, alongside name, income, SSN, address, and estimated value.

questions.title: What does not start the clock
questions.brief: The appraisal is ordered for next week.
questions.question: What starts the application for TRID timing in this sim?

options.text: Having the six items, not delivery of the appraisal

questions.explain: The clock starts when the six items are received. The appraisal is collateral work that comes after.

questions.title: Order of work
questions.brief: You can already name the borrower, the income, the SSN, the address, the value, and the loan amount.
questions.question: Can supporting documents be collected after the application exists?

options.text: No. The file must be complete before it is an application

questions.explain: The six items create the application. The rest of the file is built from there.

questions.title: What counts as a business day
questions.brief: The lender's offices in this sim are open Monday through Friday.
questions.question: For the Loan Estimate clock in this sim, which days count?
questions.explain: This sim treats an LE business day as a day the lender is open. Saturday and Sunday do not count.

questions.title: How many days
questions.brief: The application date is already on the file.
questions.question: How soon must the Loan Estimate go out?

options.text: Within three business days of application
Within three calendar days, counting Sunday

questions.explain: The rule practiced here is three business days from application, using lender-open days.

questions.title: The fourth open day
questions.brief: Someone suggests sending the LE on the fourth day the office is open.
questions.question: Is the fourth lender-open day still on time in this sim?

options.text: No. The last day is the third open day
Yes. You have a full week
Yes, if the borrower has not asked for it

questions.explain: Three open days is the deadline. The fourth open day is late.

questions.title: Two different disclosures
questions.brief: A teammate calls the early disclosure the Closing Disclosure.
questions.question: Is the Loan Estimate the same document as the Closing Disclosure?

options.text: Yes. Only the title changes at closing

questions.explain: The Loan Estimate goes out after application. The Closing Disclosure goes out before consummation. They are not the same form.

questions.title: Where the clock starts
questions.brief: The file shows an application date.
questions.question: What date starts the Loan Estimate clock?

options.text: The day the appraisal is paid

questions.explain: Three business days are counted from the application date.

questions.title: Sending it early
questions.brief: The LE is ready on day one.
questions.question: May you deliver the Loan Estimate before the last legal day?

options.text: Yes. Earlier is allowed. The rule is a deadline, not a waiting period
No. You must wait until day three
Only if the borrower is a first-time buyer

questions.explain: The third business day is the last day, not the only day.

questions.title: A revised Loan Estimate
questions.brief: A fee was known at application and was left off the first LE.
questions.question: When is a revised Loan Estimate the right tool?

options.text: For a valid changed circumstance, not to repair a fee you could have quoted correctly
Whenever a number on the LE looks inconvenient

questions.explain: A revised LE follows a valid changed circumstance. It is not a way to fix a fee that should have been on the original.

questions.title: Fees before intent
questions.brief: The borrower has the LE and has not said they want to proceed.
questions.question: Which fee can you generally charge before the borrower intends to proceed?

options.text: The appraisal and any lender fee
Any fee listed on the LE

questions.explain: Before intent to proceed, the credit-report fee is the usual exception. Other fees wait.

questions.title: Holidays in this sim
questions.brief: A weekday on the LE clock is a federal holiday.
questions.question: Does this simulator skip federal holidays when it counts Loan Estimate days?

options.text: No. Weekdays count here even if they are holidays
Yes. Every federal holiday is removed
Yes, but only Christmas and Thanksgiving

questions.explain: This sim ignores federal holidays. A weekday counts as a lender-open day. Real calendars still have to be checked outside the sim.

questions.title: The 80% line
questions.brief: You are on a conventional loan.
questions.question: When does this training sim treat conventional PMI as required?
questions.explain: Conventional loans above 80% LTV need private mortgage insurance in this sim.

questions.title: Down payment and LTV
questions.brief: The borrower is putting 20% down and financing the rest.
questions.question: What LTV is a 20% down payment?
questions.explain: LTV is the loan divided by the value. Twenty percent down leaves an 80% loan.

questions.title: How LTV is built
questions.brief: The instruments show a loan amount and a purchase price.
questions.question: How does this sim compute LTV?

options.text: Loan amount divided by purchase price

questions.explain: LTV percent is the loan amount over the price, from the shared calculation engine.

questions.title: Not the same insurance
questions.brief: Someone calls every premium PMI.
questions.question: What is the mortgage insurance on a standard FHA loan usually called?

options.text: PMI, the same product as conventional

questions.explain: FHA uses a mortgage insurance premium. Conventional PMI is a different line.

questions.title: VA is not PMI
questions.brief: The file might be VA.
questions.question: What does a VA loan use instead of conventional PMI?

options.text: A VA funding fee, unless the borrower is exempt

questions.explain: VA loans have a funding fee, with exemptions for some borrowers. They do not use conventional PMI.

questions.title: 90% conventional
questions.brief: LTV on a conventional purchase is 90%.
questions.question: Does that conventional loan need PMI?

options.text: Only if it is a second home

questions.explain: 90% is above 80%, so conventional PMI applies.

questions.title: 75% conventional
questions.brief: LTV on a conventional purchase is 75%.
questions.question: Does that conventional loan need PMI?

options.text: Yes. PMI is required on every conventional loan
Yes, because the rate is over 6%

questions.explain: 75% is at or under 80%, so conventional PMI is not required.

questions.title: No second lien
questions.brief: There is no subordinate financing on this file.
questions.question: How does CLTV compare with LTV when there is no second lien?
questions.explain: CLTV adds subordinate liens on top of the loan. With none, CLTV equals LTV.

questions.title: Do not argue with the gauge
questions.brief: LTV is over 80% and someone says to skip PMI because the payment feels fine.
questions.question: Does ignoring the LTV gauge remove conventional PMI?

options.text: Yes, after the appraisal is waived

questions.explain: PMI follows the LTV. The gauge is the reading you use.

questions.title: Fannie affordable
questions.brief: The borrower is income-limited and will live in the home. You are choosing a Fannie Mae line from this catalog.
questions.question: Which product is Fannie Mae's affordable conventional option in this catalog?
questions.explain: HomeReady is Fannie Mae. Home Possible is Freddie Mac's counterpart. HomeStyle is Fannie's renovation line.

questions.title: Freddie affordable
questions.brief: You want the Freddie Mac line that pairs with HomeReady.
questions.question: Which product is Freddie Mac's affordable option in this catalog?
questions.explain: Home Possible is Freddie Mac. CHOICEHome is Freddie's renovation line. HomeReady is Fannie.

questions.title: Fannie renovation
questions.brief: The borrower will buy the house and renovate it on a Fannie delivery.
questions.question: Which Fannie Mae line is the renovation product in this catalog?
questions.explain: HomeStyle Renovation is the Fannie renovation path. The high-LTV option is a refinance, and HomeReady is the affordable purchase and rate-term line.

questions.title: Freddie renovation
questions.brief: Same renovation idea, Freddie Mac delivery.
questions.question: Which Freddie Mac line is the renovation product in this catalog?
questions.explain: CHOICEHome is Freddie's renovation execution. Home Possible is affordable financing. Relief refinance is a rate-and-term path.

questions.title: FHA forward
questions.brief: The borrower wants a standard FHA-insured purchase and will occupy the home.
questions.question: Which line is the standard FHA forward mortgage in this catalog?
questions.explain: 203(b) is the standard FHA forward loan. Streamline refinances an existing FHA loan. Limited 203(k) adds a capped rehab.

questions.title: Existing FHA loan
questions.brief: The borrower already has an FHA loan and wants a rate-and-term refinance with a net tangible benefit.
questions.question: Which FHA line fits that file?
questions.explain: Streamline is the FHA rate-and-term refinance of an existing FHA loan, with a net tangible benefit test. It is not a purchase and not the rehab line.

questions.title: FHA rehab
questions.brief: The owner-occupant needs a limited rehab scope, not a plain purchase.
questions.question: Which FHA line is the capped rehab product in this catalog?
questions.explain: Limited 203(k) is the FHA rehab path with a capped scope. Streamline does not add renovation. IRRRL is VA.

questions.title: Veteran purchase
questions.brief: An eligible veteran will buy and occupy, and you still need the Certificate of Eligibility.
questions.question: Which line is the VA purchase in this catalog?
questions.explain: The purchase line is for a new VA-guaranteed purchase. IRRRL refinances an existing VA loan without cash out. Cash-out is its own line.

questions.title: Existing VA loan
questions.brief: The borrower already has a VA loan and wants a lower rate, not cash out.
questions.question: Which VA line is that rate-and-term refinance?
questions.explain: IRRRL is the VA interest-rate reduction refinance. Purchase is a new buy. Cash-out takes equity out and uses a lower LTV cap in this catalog.

questions.title: Rural purchase
questions.brief: The home has to sit in a USDA-eligible area, and household income has to fit the area limit.
questions.question: Which line is the USDA purchase in this catalog?
questions.explain: Guaranteed purchase is the USDA buy. Streamlined assist refinances an existing USDA loan. 203(b) is FHA.

questions.title: HomeReady LTV
questions.brief: Primary-residence purchase on HomeReady. Read this catalog, not a live guide.
questions.question: What is HomeReady's max LTV on a primary purchase in this catalog?
questions.explain: This catalog sets HomeReady max LTV on a primary purchase at 97%. 96.5% is the FHA 203(b) figure.

questions.title: HomeReady CLTV
questions.brief: HomeReady can have assistance that sits above the first mortgage.
questions.question: How do HomeReady's LTV and CLTV caps compare in this catalog?
questions.explain: HomeReady's catalog caps are 97% LTV and 105% CLTV. Home Possible uses the same pair.

questions.title: HomeReady occupancy
questions.brief: The borrower wants HomeReady on a rental property.
questions.question: Which occupancy does this catalog allow for HomeReady?
questions.explain: HomeReady in this catalog is primary residence only. Standard conforming allows primary, second home, and investment.

questions.title: Income limit
questions.brief: You are checking HomeReady before anyone promises the product.
questions.question: What income limit does this prototype use for HomeReady and Home Possible?
questions.explain: The prototype uses 80% of AMI. Low-income census tract rules can differ, so the file still needs the agency AMI lookup for the address.

questions.title: Affordable credit floors
questions.brief: HomeReady and Home Possible are both on the board.
questions.question: How do the catalog minimum credit scores compare?
questions.explain: In this catalog HomeReady's minimum is 620 and Home Possible's minimum is 660. Investor overlays can be tighter than either.

questions.title: Standard conforming occupancy
questions.brief: The loan is standard conventional conforming, not an affordable line.
questions.question: Which occupancies does standard conforming allow in this catalog?
questions.explain: Fannie and Freddie standard conforming in this catalog allow primary, second home, and investment. Affordable lines do not.

questions.title: FHA 203(b) LTV
questions.brief: Primary purchase, FHA 203(b).
questions.question: What is the max LTV for FHA 203(b) primary purchase in this catalog?
questions.explain: FHA 203(b) is 96.5% LTV in this catalog. 97% is the conventional affordable cap. 100% is VA purchase and USDA purchase.

questions.title: FHA 203(b) credit
questions.brief: You are comparing agency floors in the catalog, before overlays.
questions.question: What minimum credit score does this catalog list for FHA 203(b)?
questions.explain: FHA 203(b) and FHA streamline list 580. Limited 203(k) lists 620. USDA lists 640. Lenders often overlay higher floors.

questions.title: VA purchase LTV
questions.brief: VA-guaranteed purchase, primary residence.
questions.question: What max LTV does this catalog give a VA purchase?
questions.explain: VA purchase and VA IRRRL are 100% LTV here. VA cash-out is 90%.

questions.title: VA cash-out LTV
questions.brief: The veteran wants cash out, not an IRRRL.
questions.question: What max LTV does this catalog give VA cash-out?
questions.explain: VA cash-out stops at 90% LTV and 90% CLTV in this catalog. Do not reuse the purchase cap.

questions.title: Investor A credit floor
questions.brief: Conventional primary occupancy. The score is 645. Investor A's overlay is a hard stop below 660.
questions.question: What does that overlay mean for this file?

options.text: Investor A is a hard stop. Move investors or improve the score
It still fits because the agency floor is 620
The overlay applies only to investment occupancy

questions.explain: Investor A's conventional primary overlay is a hard stop under 660. The agency 620 floor does not override that investor.

questions.title: Investment DTI overlay
questions.brief: Investment occupancy, conventional, back-end DTI 48%. Investor A caps investment DTI at 45% as a hard stop.
questions.question: Which call matches the overlay?

options.text: Hard stop at Investor A. Change the program or get an exception path
The catalog's 50% DTI max always wins
That cap is a USDA rule

questions.explain: Investor A's investment DTI cap is 45% and a hard stop. The agency max in the catalog is not a substitute for the overlay.

questions.title: Renovation DTI
questions.brief: HomeStyle or CHOICEHome, not standard conforming.
questions.question: What max DTI does this catalog list for those renovation lines?
questions.explain: HomeStyle and CHOICEHome list 45% max DTI. Standard conforming lists 50%. VA purchase lists 60%.

questions.title: Renovation LTV
questions.brief: Primary purchase on HomeStyle or CHOICEHome.
questions.question: What max LTV does this catalog list for those renovation lines?
questions.explain: Both renovation lines cap primary purchase LTV and CLTV at 95% in this catalog.

questions.title: High-LTV and relief refis
questions.brief: Fannie's high-LTV refinance option and Freddie's relief refinance are on the list.
questions.question: Which purpose does this catalog allow for those two lines?
questions.explain: Both are rate-and-term refinances. They are not purchase products and they are not cash-out.

questions.title: USDA property types
questions.brief: The collateral is a 3-unit property. The line would be USDA guaranteed.
questions.question: Which property types does USDA allow in this catalog?

options.text: Single family, PUD, and condo. Not 2- to 4-unit
The same list as Fannie, including 2- to 4-unit

questions.explain: USDA rows in this catalog allow single family, PUD, and condo. They do not list 2-unit, 3-unit, or 4-unit.

questions.title: Limited 203(k) leverage
questions.brief: FHA Limited 203(k), with rehab financing in the stack.
questions.question: What LTV and CLTV caps does this catalog list for Limited 203(k)?
questions.explain: Limited 203(k) keeps the 96.5% LTV and allows CLTV up to 110% in this catalog. Plain 203(b) keeps both at 96.5%.

questions.title: FHA manual reserves
questions.brief: Investor B, FHA, manual underwrite. The overlay wants reserves.
questions.question: What reserve floor does Investor B put on an FHA manual underwrite?

options.text: At least 3 months, and a shortfall needs an exception

questions.explain: Investor B's FHA manual overlay is 3 months of reserves and is marked requires-exception, not a silent pass.

questions.title: VA DTI by purpose
questions.brief: You are comparing VA purchase with VA cash-out in this catalog.
questions.question: How do the catalog max DTI figures compare?
questions.explain: VA purchase and IRRRL list 60% max DTI. VA cash-out lists 50%. Residual income is still a VA test this prototype does not score.

questions.title: Sample conforming limits
questions.brief: The tool's 2026 sample table has Dallas County and Orange County, California. Confirm the live year at FHFA before you rely on it.
questions.question: Which sample row is the baseline 1-unit limit, and which is the high-cost 1-unit limit?

options.text: Dallas is the high-cost row at $1,149,825

questions.explain: The bundled sample marks Dallas as not high-cost at $806,500 for 1 unit, and Orange County, California as high-cost at $1,149,825. Those rows are sample data for the analyzer.

questions.title: Back-end DTI
questions.brief: The back-end gauge is the one with every debt on it.
questions.question: What is back-end DTI?

options.text: Total monthly debt divided by gross monthly income
Housing payment divided by the loan amount

questions.explain: Back-end DTI puts principal, interest, taxes, insurance, and other monthly debts over gross monthly income.

questions.title: Front-end DTI
questions.brief: The housing gauge is on the panel.
questions.question: What is front-end DTI?

options.text: Housing payment divided by gross monthly income
All debts, including the car, divided by income

questions.explain: Front-end DTI is the housing payment over gross monthly income. The car and other debts sit in the back-end number.

questions.title: Shorter term
questions.brief: Someone offers a 15-year term to make the file look stronger.
questions.question: What does a shorter term do to principal and interest, and then to DTI?

options.text: It raises the payment and can make DTI worse
It cuts the payment in half
It does not change the payment

questions.explain: A shorter amortization raises principal and interest. Higher payment, higher DTI.

questions.title: Paying off a debt
questions.brief: An installment payment is in the back-end ratio. Assets can cover the balance.
questions.question: How can paying that debt off from assets help DTI?

options.text: The monthly payment comes off the debts

questions.explain: Removing the payment lowers total monthly debt. The assets used to pay it off also lower reserves, so read both gauges.

questions.title: Adding income
questions.brief: A co-borrower's income can be added if it qualifies.
questions.question: How does qualifying co-borrower income change DTI?

options.text: It raises the income denominator and can lower the ratio

questions.explain: DTI falls when qualifying income rises and the debts stay put.

questions.title: This sim's ceiling
questions.brief: The underwriting checkpoint has its own target.
questions.question: What back-end ceiling does this flight use as the practice target?
questions.explain: This checkpoint wants the file at 45% or below. That is a training target. The product catalog's standard conforming max is 50%, and VA purchase lists 60%.

questions.title: Do not mix the numbers
questions.brief: A teammate quotes 50% because that is the standard conforming catalog max.
questions.question: Is that 50% the same number as this sim's practice ceiling?

options.text: No. The practice ceiling on this checkpoint is 45%
Yes. They are the same rule

questions.explain: Keep the two numbers apart. This flight practices to 45%. Standard conforming in the catalog lists 50%.

questions.title: Reserve months
questions.brief: The reserves gauge is in months.
questions.question: How does this sim turn assets into reserve months?

options.text: Liquid assets divided by the housing payment

questions.explain: Reserve months are assets over the housing payment, from the calculation engine.

questions.title: Income that counts
questions.brief: Someone wants to add income that is not documented as qualifying.
questions.question: Which income lowers DTI on this file?

options.text: Qualifying income that is actually on the file

questions.explain: Only income that qualifies and is entered on the file moves the ratio.

questions.title: Holding pattern: the deposit
questions.brief: The bank statement shows a deposit that is not payroll.
questions.question: How do you clear that condition?

options.text: A letter of explanation and source documents
Drop the bank account from the file
Ignore it because an automated system already approved

questions.explain: A large deposit that is not payroll has to be sourced and explained. Dropping an account you need, or skipping an open condition, does not clear the file.

questions.title: Do not drop the account
questions.brief: The unsourced deposit is in the account that holds the reserves.
questions.question: Does removing that account from the file clear the condition?

options.text: No. You still need the funds, and the deposit still has to be sourced
Yes. If the account is gone, the condition is gone

questions.explain: Taking the account off the file hides the funds you are using. It does not explain the deposit.

questions.title: Approval is not clearance
questions.brief: An automated findings report says approve, and a deposit condition is still open.
questions.question: Does that approval clear the condition?

options.text: Yes. Approve means the condition list is optional

questions.explain: Findings do not erase an open condition. Clearance is the sourced paper.

questions.title: Gift funds
questions.brief: Part of the funds to close is a gift.
questions.question: What does a gift condition usually need?

options.text: Donor ability and a transfer trail
Only a text message from the donor
Nothing, if the borrower is related to the donor

questions.explain: Gift funds need evidence the donor could give the money and that it moved into the file.

questions.title: Wrong document
questions.brief: The open item is an unexplained deposit.
questions.question: Which document answers a deposit condition?

options.text: Source documents for that deposit, not a verification of employment
A verification of employment by itself

questions.explain: A verification of employment supports the job. The deposit needs its own source paper.

questions.title: Collateral versus credit
questions.brief: The appraisal asks for a repair.
questions.question: What kind of condition is that?
questions.explain: Repair items from the appraisal are collateral conditions. They are not cleared with a deposit letter.

questions.title: Still open
questions.brief: One condition has no document behind it.
questions.question: Can the file go clear to close with that condition open?

options.text: Yes, if the score is high
Yes, if closing is this week

questions.explain: An open condition holds the file. Clear to close means the list is satisfied.

questions.title: Sourcing
questions.brief: The borrower explains the deposit out loud and offers no paper.
questions.question: Is that enough to source it?

options.text: No. Sourcing is a paper trail
Yes. A verbal explanation is the source
Yes, after the CD is out

questions.explain: The letter tells the story. The statements or transfer records show the money.

questions.title: Paying a debt with unsourced cash
questions.brief: The borrower wants to pay off the car with a deposit that is not sourced.
questions.question: What can that do to the file?

options.text: Add a sourcing condition instead of quietly fixing DTI

questions.explain: A payoff only helps if the money is sourced. Unsourced cash becomes its own condition.

questions.title: The list is the work
questions.brief: The underwriter published a condition list.
questions.question: What is that list?

options.text: The clearance list, not optional commentary
Suggestions you can skip if the payment looks fine
A copy of the Loan Estimate

questions.explain: Each open item has to be satisfied before the file is clear to close.

questions.title: How early the borrower has it
questions.brief: Consummation is the closing date on this file.
questions.question: When must the borrower receive the Closing Disclosure?

options.text: At least three business days before consummation
Any time in the application week

questions.explain: Three business days before consummation is the rule this sim practices.

questions.title: CD business days
questions.brief: This clock is not the Loan Estimate clock.
questions.question: Which days count as Closing Disclosure business days in this sim?

options.text: Only Monday through Friday, same as the LE
Sunday counts and Saturday does not

questions.explain: For the CD, this sim counts every day except Sunday. Saturday counts. The LE clock is lender-open days and skips both weekend days.

questions.title: Holidays still unmodeled
questions.brief: A weekday before closing is a federal holiday.
questions.question: Does this sim remove federal holidays from the CD count?

options.text: Yes. All federal holidays are skipped
Yes, but only when they fall on Saturday

questions.explain: Holidays are not modeled. Outside this sim, the real calendar still has to be checked.

questions.title: The day before
questions.brief: Closing is tomorrow. The borrower does not have the CD yet.
questions.question: Is delivery the day before closing on time in this sim?

options.text: No. That is inside the three-business-day window
Yes, if the LE was on time

questions.explain: The latest day is three business days before consummation, not the day before.

questions.title: Which date is consummation
questions.brief: The file shows an application date and a closing date.
questions.question: Which date is consummation for this CD question?

options.text: The day the LE was sent

questions.explain: Count backward from the closing date on the file.

questions.title: A new wait
questions.brief: The CD is already out, and a material change shows up.
questions.question: Which change can start a new three-day wait?

options.text: An APR increase past tolerance, a product change, or adding a prepayment penalty
Any typo in the mailing address

questions.explain: A new waiting period can apply when the APR increases beyond tolerance, the loan product changes, or a prepayment penalty is added.

questions.title: Do not swap the forms
questions.brief: The Loan Estimate went out at application.
questions.question: Does that Loan Estimate satisfy the Closing Disclosure timing rule?

options.text: Yes. One disclosure covers both clocks

questions.explain: The LE and the CD are different disclosures with different clocks.

questions.title: Earlier than the last day
questions.brief: The CD can be sent more than three business days before closing.
questions.question: Is earlier delivery allowed?

options.text: Yes. The rule is the latest day, not the only day
No. It must be exactly three days before

questions.explain: Earlier receipt is fine. The question on this flight is the latest day that still works.

questions.title: Sunday
questions.brief: You are counting CD business days and you land on a Sunday.
questions.question: Does Sunday count in this sim?

options.text: Only if the lender is open

questions.explain: Sunday is skipped on the CD count in this sim. Saturday is not.

questions.title: What the tier is
questions.brief: The risk gauge has a color and a word.
questions.question: What is that risk tier?

options.text: A training color from DTI, reserves, and LTV, not an underwriting decision

questions.explain: The tier is a coarse UI color. It does not approve the loan and it does not pick a product line.

questions.title: DTI points
questions.brief: Back-end DTI is 46%.
questions.question: How many risk points does that add in this sim?
questions.explain: DTI at or above 45% adds 2 points. DTI at or above 40% and under 45% adds 1.

questions.title: Reserve points
questions.brief: Reserves are 3 months.
questions.question: How many risk points does that add?
questions.explain: Reserves under 2 months add 2 points. Reserves under 4 months add 1. Three months is 1 point.

questions.title: LTV points
questions.brief: LTV is 92%.
questions.question: How many risk points does that add?
questions.explain: LTV over 95% adds 2 points. LTV over 90% and up to 95% adds 1. 92% is 1 point.

questions.title: Two points
questions.brief: The three gauges add up to 2 points.
questions.question: Which tier is 2 points?
questions.explain: Two or three points is medium. Four or more is high. Under two is low.

questions.title: Four points
questions.brief: The gauges add up to 4 points.
questions.question: Which tier is 4 points?
questions.explain: Four points is the high tier. Medium starts at 2.

questions.title: What the tier reads
questions.brief: Rate, term, and credit score are on the file.
questions.question: Which inputs does the risk tier actually use?

options.text: Back-end DTI, reserve months, and LTV
Credit score and the note rate

questions.explain: The engine scores back-end DTI, reserves, and LTV only.

questions.title: Not a submission
questions.brief: The flight reaches funding.
questions.question: Does finishing this sim submit the file to DU or LPA?

options.text: Yes. Funding here is an AUS run
Yes, but only at Captain difficulty

questions.explain: This is a synthetic training flight. It does not run AUS and it does not fund a real loan.

questions.title: Where the analyzer is
questions.brief: You want the product-fit grid from the GSE analyzer.
questions.question: How do you open that analyzer from this flight?

options.text: The pilot-report button links to it. This score does not fill that page
The flight result is written onto the analyzer automatically
The risk tier is the analyzer's best-fit product

questions.explain: The report has a button that opens the GSE analyzer as its own tool. The flight score stays here.
